S1.hook: When does this patient go home?
S1.dek: Houston Methodist compared two ways of answering it, and published which one was closer when accurate estimations are most actionable for bed management.

S2.dek: The hospital's own staff, and a commercial clinician-assisted tool integrated with the EHR, over every inpatient encounter discharged in the window below.

S3.dek: At admission the case managers and the tool sat within a fraction of a day of each other on error. Both marks are out at that distance, and the air between here and there is what a reader has to see through.
labels: MATCHED THE EXACT DATE, AT ADMISSION

S4.hook: On the last day, they were not
labels: WITHIN ONE DAY OF THE TRUE DATE 24 HOURS BEFORE DISCHARGE

S5.dek: Mean absolute error in days. The two never meet, and the gap between them is wider at the door than it was at the earlier reading.

S6.dek: The strong admission correlation did not persist nearer discharge and should not be interpreted as evidence that the tool captured the same information clinicians use throughout the stay.
labels: The study's authors, on their own result

S7.dek: Estimates were part of usual care and visible to care teams, so they may be partly self-fulfilling and, in the authors' own word, advantaged nearer discharge.
labels: Accessible in the EHR but not enabled automatically. Nothing was shining on this one.
The study's authors, against their own result

S8.dek: No baseline patient demographic data were available.
labels: THE STUDY FOLLOWED THE SQUIRE REPORTING GUIDELINE

S9.dek: The authors say what has to happen before anyone decides the tool is worth what it takes to run it.
labels: PUBLISHED SEPTEMBER 3RD, 2026 OPEN ACCESS, AND FREE TO READ TODAY
